content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices after bullish sentiment spikes, especially following auction events; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% post-spike.
- Underestimates prices when sentiment turns bearish or sentiment is neutral, particularly after consecutive bullish events; add 3–7% upward bias to offset mean reversion.
- Forecast drifts upward after consecutive auction events (supply net negative) — adjust downward by 2–5% per event to reflect supply pressure.
- When sentiment is mixed or negative, model tends to ignore recent low prices; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- Overshoots after high volatility periods (e.g., 70+ price spikes) — cap forecast slope at 0.5–1.0% per day after spike to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment history shows 2+ consecutive bullish events followed by bearish, model overcorrects; apply 1–3% downward bias to prevent over-adjustment.
- For auctions with supply net >0, model underestimates price drop — add 2–5% upward bias to reflect auction-driven volatility.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 3–6% to reflect sentiment-driven correction.
